encounters.cc: Intraoperative hypotension, tachycardia, and wheezing during elective cholecystectomy

lines: Intraoperative hypotension, tachycardia, and wheezing during elective cholecystectomy

The patient returns for elective cholecystectomy 18 months following her diagnosis of cholelithiasis, amid ongoing management of hypertension, status post transsphenoidal resection for Cushing disease, and recent treatment for bilateral breast pathology.

Approximately 30 minutes into the procedure, the anesthesiologist notes that the patient's blood pressure has dropped to 85/50 mmHg from a baseline of 130/80 mmHg, and her heart rate has increased to 110 bpm.
The patient is also noted to have wheezing on auscultation.
The surgical team is alerted, and upon inspection under the surgical drapes, widespread urticaria is observed.
The patient's oxygen saturation has decreased to 92% on FiO2 of 0.5.
